7: One examines a zav - with regard to food and with regard to drink, with regard to sickness, with regard to jumping, with regard to a burden, and with regard to a[n arousing] sight, and with regard to the thought [of a woman], in case he saw [the discharge] due to one of these [factors]. [Any of those] would make him a victim of circumstances beyond his control,  and [thereby] pure. As the Torah says, "from his flesh" [Leviticus 15:2] -- [that is], on its own, and not due to [other] circumstances beyond his control. Whereas a woman becomes impure even due to circumstances beyond her control, as is stated in chapter "Samaritan Girls" [Niddah 36b:13]: "When the verse states: “And if a woman has an issue of her blood" [Leviticus 15:25], it is referring to circumstances beyond her control.
